newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - June 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - June 13.

text.p: Wool Board faces loss of monopoly: The Wool Board faces losing its statutory monopoly on the marketing of wool because more than 50 percent of the industry opposes paying the board's funding levy. Page 1.
NZ Post sets sights on Freightways: New Zealand Post is eyeing the private courier business put on the block by millionaire Alan Gibbs' Freightways Group. Page 1.

Report says Companies Office records so bad 34 staff needed: Half the records on the Companies Office database are inacurate, according to a report leaked to Labour Party front bencher Trevor Mallard. Page 3.
Watchdog clears Isocnz: The Internet Society (Isocnz) has been cleared of possible breaches of the Commerce Act over its Internet domain-name registration scheme. Page 3.

Fay Richwhite retains option to frustrate wine-box report: Fay Richwhite & Co could still seek to delay or stop winebox commissioner Sir Ronald Davison from reporting contrary to a public assurance it gave in April. Page 4.

Economy can expect little help from rural sector: With dairy farmers facing another slump in returns and the meat and wool sector largely stagnant, there is little prospect of rural New Zealand boosting the flagging national economy over the next year or so. Page 8.

Coalition demolishes barriers to $5bn extra spending as it enters pre-Budget spin mode: Desptie rhetoric about prudent and conservative economic management, the coalition's extra $5 billion spending seems to be protected from other economic factors. Page 10.

Winebox five counter-attack commissioner: Fay Richwhite, Brierley Investments and European Pacific will seek an injunction gagging winebox commissioner Sir Ron Davison from presenting his report to the Governor-General, unless the courts can deal with their judicial challenge to the conduct of the winebox inquiry before Sir Ron's August reporting date. Page 1.

Tranz Rail shunts Willy Horts out of TeNZ: Tranz Rail's share price leapt 16 cents and Wilson and Horton's shares plunged 30 cents this week following a stock exchange announcement foreshadowing the TeNZ's fund's first portfolio adjustment. Page 1.

BIL aims to break up LWR: Brierley Investments has abandoned its search for a joint venture partner in its clothing company, Canterbury International. But BIL is still keen to break up the parent company, LWR Industries, and sell Canterbury. Page 2.

Business Rountable calls for review of compulsory disclosure: Within two days of the Commerce Commission warning the public against a retirement savings scheme, the Business Roundtable is reiterating its call for a loosening of state regulation of the finance industry. Page 2.

Second investigation for Robins: The current Serious Fraud Office inquiry into former ACC boss Gavin Robins is not the first time a government watchdog has looked into his financial dealings with the corporation. page 3.

TVNZ cutting cord on near-profitable station, critics cry: Horizon Pacific Television, dumped this week as a commercial failure by owner TVNZ, was ahead of sales targets and had stations near profitability, according to sources close to Horizon. Page 6.
